title: Comparison sorts cannot beat n log n, and it is provable
body: Any sort that learns only by comparing pairs is a decision tree, and telling apart all n-factorial orders needs at least log2(n!) questions, which grows like n log n. That is why comparison sorts stop at n log n, while special sorts that exploit the keys themselves, like counting sort, can go faster.
source_hint: Decision-tree lower bound (CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms)
